structure: Nebraska Social Studies Standards (approved Nov 8, 2019). Front matter: contents and 'Standards Structure' (u6-u30). Then one section per grade K-5 (titled 'Kindergarten', 'Grade 1'...), a Middle School Overview (intro + 3-column 6th/7th/8th summary table), Grades 6, 7, 8 sections, and a high school band (HS = 9-12) divided into High School Civics, Economics, Geography and History. Each grade section opens with a 'Grade Level Summary and Theme' narrative, then four disciplines (Civics, Economics, Geography, History). Within a discipline are big ideas (e.g. Forms and Functions of Government, Civic Participation; Economic Decision Making, Financial Literacy, Exchange and Markets, National Economy, Global Economy; Location and Place, Regions, Human-Environment Interaction, Movement, Geospatial Skills and Geo-literacy; Change/Continuity/Context, Multiple Perspectives, Historical Analysis and Interpretation, Historical Inquiry and Research). Standards are coded 'SS G.D.S' (grade.discipline 1-4.standard, e.g. SS 3.1.1; K uses K.1.1; HS uses HS.1.1) with indicators 'SS G.D.S.a' (e.g. SS 3.1.1.a); HS History standards carry '(US)' or '(WLD)' tags. Indicators are followed by 'For example: ...' lists (examples). Many tables are extracted as fragmented cells. Grades come from section headings and code prefixes.

issues: Extraction is table-fragmented throughout: many standards and their 'For example' text are split across table-cell units (e.g. u86-u90, u100-u103, u738-u745, u946-u957). Units with no SS code or 'For example' marker were labeled by position: fragments following a 'For example' unit (or whose 'For example:' prefix was lost, e.g. u758-u759, u772-u775, u866-u867, u877, u905-u909, u971-u975, u1024-u1026, u1130-u1132, u1288-u1290) are labeled examples; continuations of standard text (e.g. u102, u177, u202, u274, u370, u476-u477, u615, u739-u742) are labeled standards.

Many table cells are duplicated in the extraction (same standard text appears twice, e.g. u89/u90, u484, u660/u661, u663/u664, u681, u695, u719/u720, u877/u879, u955/u956). Both copies labeled the same way; text order may be scrambled.

u90, u202, u236, u1407: mixed or fragmentary units labeled standards (u90 is a duplicate cut-off copy of K.4.1.b; u236 contains the end of SS 2.2.4.b plus its example; u1407 is the World History course heading).

Units that combine a standard with its 'For example' text (very common, e.g. u59, u73, u119, u1228, and most HS units) are labeled standards (units not split). Units combining several indicators (e.g. u73, u306, u390, u1307, u1322, u1331, u1338) cover multiple codes.

Grade Level Summary and Theme / HS 'Summary' units (u35, u116, u208, u302, u395, u509, u735, u893, u1094, u1282, u1313, u1352, u1384) mix the theme title with a content narrative and some end with the discipline heading (e.g. 'Civics'); labeled examples (narrative describing what students study) rather than standards. Alternative: standards for the theme title.

u627-u730 (Middle School Overview table, pages 35-36): 3-column grid (6th C1-C3, 7th C4-C6, 8th C7-C9) of standard-level statements (6.x.x / 7.x.x / 8.x.x) that repeat the per-grade standards in the Grade 6/7/8 sections; grades assigned by SS code prefix, else by column; strand-name cells (Civics, Economics, Geography, History) get 6-8. Cells such as u660/u661 and u663/u664 are split or duplicated across columns. u627 intro labeled backup.

State guide lists HS topics as Civics, Economics, Geography, History strands; the document has no separate HS courses: HS standards are one 9-12 band organized by discipline (SS HS.1.x Civics, HS.2.x Economics, HS.3.x Geography, HS.4.x History). Civics, Economics, Geography labeled course null, grades 9-12; the History strand has two course-like sub-sections coded (US) and (WLD), labeled course 'United States History (Progressive Era – Present)' and 'World History (1500 CE – Present)' (u1385-u1406, u1407-u1423); the History strand title/summary (u1383-u1384) are course null.

HS History uses the same code numbers for both sub-sections (HS.4.1 (US) vs HS.4.1 (WLD)); distinguished only by the (US)/(WLD) tags in the text and the sub-section heading; unit boundaries confirm no overlap.

Pages 1 and 3 contain images only (cover; numbering-system figure after u30): no units. Page 6-7 etc. 'Standards numbering' key image not extracted. Some text truncated at cell edge (u190 'patriotic s', u200 'wa', u903 'thei', u873 'historica', u895 'governmenta').

Recurring truncation of strand headings: some big-idea headings are separate units (u83-u84, u170-u172), some fused with the first standard (u36, u41, u49), and 'Not addressed at this level' placeholders (e.g. u56, u139, u334, u532-u533) are labeled standards because they carry SS codes.
Reviewer: NE high school is one 9-12 band organized by strand (Civics, Economics, Geography, History US/WLD); no course rows.
